sources.citation: OLAC listing for Tocho [taz] (Wayback 2025-11-11) and SIL Language & Culture Archives search for [taz] (Wayback 2015).
sources.note: Catalogue pages only: list Rosetta Swadesh list, OPSL 9 (Spronk 2004), Norton & Alaki 2015, Glottolog, PHOIBLE, Ethnologue. No open deposit of the 2013 chapter.

sources.citation: Spronk, Tanya. 2004. A brief description of the current Talodi orthographies. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 119-126. Khartoum/Nairobi: SIL-Sudan.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing. Covers consonants, vowels/ATR harmony and tone only; for Tocco: sec. 5.5 p.124 'Jacob (1996) has reported some minimal pairs for High and Low tone in Tocco. The tone is not currently marked in the orthography'. No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Tocho language' (raw wikitext, fetched sources 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Tertiary; consonant notes citing Alaki & Norton 2013:178-180; nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Quint, Nicolas. 2020. Kordofanian. In Vossen & Dimmendaal (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of African Languages. OUP (author version halshs-03093501).
sources.note: Tocho appears only in lexical comparisons; family-level remark that Kordofanian languages are tonal; nothing on Tocho stress.

sources.citation: Smits, Heleen. 2017. A grammar of Lumun, a Kordofanian language of Sudan. Utrecht: LOT (465).
sources.note: About Lumun, not Tocho; Tocho mentioned only for classification, neighbours and loans. Nothing on Tocho prosody.

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Thomas Kuku Alaki. 2015. The Talodi languages: a comparative-historical analysis. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 11: 47-161. Juba: SIL.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Explicitly declines to treat prosody (sec. 3.2.5, p.107): 'We omit analysis of prosodic features for lack of data and for lack of functional load'; notes two tone levels across Talodi languages with rare minimal pairs, conditioned vowel length (citing Alaki & Norton 2013). No stress statement for Tocho or any Talodi language.
Lists 27 segments plus H and L tones; no stress information.

sources.citation: Alaki, Thomas Kuku & Russell Norton. 2013. Tocho phonology and orthography. In Thilo C. Schadeberg & Roger M. Blench (eds.), Nuba Mountain Language Studies, 177-194. Cologne: Ruediger Koeppe. ISBN 978-3-89645-427-0.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: Harvard print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan); the journal or volume is held, not the item itself: WID WID-LC PL8571.N83 2013
sources.note: The only dedicated published phonology of Tocho (18 pp.); cited by Norton & Alaki 2015 for conditioned vowel length, so it treats suprasegmentals at least in part; most likely place for any stress/accent statement.
